title: An HF-ordering is over the set it closes
source_title: The elementary theory of free Steiner triple systems

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line

standard_prerequisites.name: HF-ordering over a subset
standard_prerequisites.statement: An ordering is over A when every element outside A has at most one pair of smaller elements forming a block with it.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the property the lemma establishes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Closure of a subset
standard_prerequisites.statement: The closure of A under the ordering is the smallest set containing A and closed under forming blocks whose other members are already present and smaller.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis is that A equals its own closure.

core_obligations: Assume the order is not over A and extract an element outside A together with two blocks witnessing the failure, choosing four distinct elements each of which is either below that element or inside A (source line 348).

Normalise the names so that one of the four is below another, and show that the lower one must be below the chosen element, since otherwise it lies in A and the element below it would be in A because A is closed (source line 348).
Repeat the argument with the second block to obtain a second element below the chosen element, contradicting that the order is an HF-ordering (source line 348).

proof_roadmap.step: Extract the two witnessing blocks and normalise.
Show each witness is below the chosen element and reach the contradiction.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 346-347: if an order is an HF-ordering of B and A equals its own closure, then the order is an HF-ordering of B over A. The proof (source lines 348-349) is a contradiction argument whose steps the statement hides: from the failure of the property one extracts an element outside A and two distinct blocks containing it, each of whose other members is either below it or in A; one then has to show, for each block, that the relevant member is below the chosen element, because the opposite would place an element below it inside A, and only then does the closure hypothesis produce the contradiction with the defining condition of an HF-ordering.
